name: Brioni
why: Roman tailoring, made to measure and ready to wear, at the top of the market.
origin: Founded in Rome in 1945 by Nazareno Fonticoli and Gaetano Savini.

notes.ital: Rome, 1945, and the first house to put men's tailoring on a runway. It still runs a tailoring school at Penne that trains its own cutters, which is a rarer thing than the marketing suggests.
notes.boat: The tailoring you change into once the tender has brought you in — the boat is the transport, not the occasion.

notes.craft: Brioni says its Penne atelier, opened 1959, still makes 'a large proportion of our production', and press puts about 1,000 tailors across Penne, Montebello di Bertona and Civitella Casanova. That is owned making for tailoring, but the brand's own wording stops short of the whole range, and shoes, knitwear and leather goods are undocumented.

cities: 7 stores, including Bal Harbour, Beverly Hills, Dallas · department stores and independent menswear shops, and its own site

marks: House fabric names: Zefiro, Trama (weave), Iride. Licensed: Escorial wool (Escorial is a third-party wool trademark). Generic: water-repellent, waterproof, membrane, technical fabric, vicuna. NO trademark symbols anywhere on the site.

craft_evidence.owned_d: Tailoring: brioni.com art-of-tailoring page: 1959 'first industrial sized tailoring atelier in Penne, Italy'; 'Today, the bond with Penne remains as does a large proportion of our production.' Wikipedia (citing WWD 2021): 1,000 tailors in production facilities in Penne, Montebello di Bertona and Civitella Casanova; tailoring school in Penne since 1985 (NYT T Magazine 2014). WWD 2021: industrial plan scaling back the three sites. Brioni is a Kering house; site facilities are Brioni's. Shoes, knitwear, leather goods making not documented.
